seo.title: About ODD — why we exist and what we do
seo.description: ODD exists to connect Finland's creative and cultural fields with business and wider society — while building better conditions for creative work itself.

title: Creativity belongs closer to the centre.
intro: ODD exists to connect Finland's creative and cultural fields with business and wider society — while building better conditions for creative work itself.
argument: Creative people shape culture, meaning, ideas, experiences and how society imagines what comes next. Those capabilities increasingly matter far beyond the creative fields.

Yet the people working with them, and the structures around them, still often sit in separate rooms. Creative work is usually built project by project, grant by grant, production by production — brilliant work with fragile continuity around it. Business and institutions, meanwhile, too rarely spend real time with the people shaping culture.
ODD exists to bring those rooms closer together — creating better conditions for creative work itself, while creating more ways for creative expertise and the rest of society to meet.

Finland already has real creative talent. The open question is what gets built around it. As execution gets cheaper through technology and AI, things like imagination, taste, cultural understanding and the ability to create meaning become more valuable, not less. A good city shouldn't only function — it should also be a place where interesting things can happen. ODD is one practical attempt to move in that direction, not the whole answer.

story.title: How we got here.

milestones.title: New Nordic Way rf founded
milestones.body: New Nordic Way rf is founded in Helsinki — the organisational home for an idea that hadn't fully taken shape yet.

milestones.title: Finding the gap
milestones.body: An idea starts forming around a simple observation: Finland has extraordinary creative people and organisations, but the structures connecting them to each other — and to the rest of society — remain fragmented.

milestones.title: ODDfest, the first experiment
milestones.body: ODDfest becomes the first major public experiment — proof that there's real appetite for bringing creative fields together differently, and connecting them with new audiences, organisations and each other. Around 2,600 participants, 350+ contributors and 70+ partners took part, reaching over a million people in total.

milestones.title: Beyond one event
milestones.body: The idea starts expanding beyond a single event. ODDference develops the professional, business-facing side; Creative Week experiments with a distributed, city-wide model; and ODDspace gives the work a physical, year-round home.

milestones.title: A clearer structure
milestones.body: The direction becomes clearer: ODDfest becomes Helsinki's creative week, ODDference becomes the centrally produced professional experience, ODDspace continues year-round, and a growing network of partnerships and projects create further ways to take part. This is where ODD is heading — not yet where it is.

story.legalNote: ODD is operated by New Nordic Way rf, a Finnish non-profit association based in Helsinki.

howWeMakeItHappen.title: Turning the idea into something real.
howWeMakeItHappen.intro: Events create moments. Spaces create continuity. Relationships and projects let things keep developing.

pillars.title: Events
pillars.body: ODDfest and ODDference create visibility, encounters and momentum — bringing different people, ideas and practices into the same moments. ODDfest opens an open, city-wide context for creative activity; ODDference creates a deliberately curated professional environment where creative expertise meets business and society.

pillars.title: Spaces
pillars.body: ODDspace gives people somewhere to work, meet and keep things developing between individual events and projects — continuity for work that would otherwise stop and restart every time.

pillars.title: Relationships & projects
pillars.body: ODDnetwork, partnerships and project-based work create ways for organisations and people to continue a relationship beyond one event — taking things further once the first conversation has happened.

howWeMakeItHappen.principlesTitle: A few things we try to hold onto.

principles.title: Make room for creativity
principles.body: We try to create conditions where other people can bring their own work, ideas and expertise — not make everything ourselves.

principles.title: Bring different worlds closer
principles.body: The point isn't to protect the line between creative fields and the rest of society. It's to make crossing it normal.

principles.title: Participation over spectatorship
principles.body: ODD works best when people are actually building and taking part, not just watching something happen to them.

principles.title: People are not the product
principles.body: Creative people are not a talent inventory for companies, and companies are not simply funding sources. Both are participants.

principles.title: Good intentions need good economics
principles.body: If something is meant to last, the economics need to work for the people actually making it — not just for the idea behind it.
